objective: Re-test the standardized-unexpected-earnings (SUE) event signal (reports/research/signal-cards/pead_sue_eps_event.json / pead_sue_eps_event.md) with visible_at moved from the first NYSE session after the 10-Q/10-K filing date to the first NYSE session after the 8-K Item 2.02 earnings-release exhibit's EDGAR acceptanceDateTime. This is task T-20260928-14 / dir:pead_xbrl_8k_llm's accounting-only stage (reports/research/control/registry-backfill-2026-09-28.md Job B, reports/research/control/autonomous-queue.md lines 77-85), reusing the existing fundamentals-v1 signal-card pipeline (open_composer/research/signal_card.py, event mode) and its built-in redated placebo unchanged; the SUE value itself (sue_eps, Foster-Olsen-Shevlin 1984 seasonal random walk) is not recomputed, only the timestamp that makes it tradable moves earlier.
target_regime_and_horizon: Same universe and horizon as the refuted card: PIT top-3000-by-dollar-ADV broad universe, close >= $5, event = sue_eps >= 2.0 at its own usable session, primary horizon 20 trading days (60 also reported), long-only, next-open fill, 10/20bp per side. Window is now bounded by 8-K Item-2.02 acceptance-timestamp data availability: data/features/earnings_events/{2024,2025,2026}.parquet covers 2024-01-02 through 2026-09-17 only (16,015 8-K/2.02 rows, 1,448 tickers, 14,923 with fetched exhibit text) -- built under docs/plan-earnings-text-forward-test-2026-09-22.zh.md T1, itself already sourced against data.sec.gov's submissions API and EDGAR fair-access rules. The refuted card's 'full' window (2016-2026) cannot be reproduced under the 8-K-timestamp definition; this iteration's 'full' and '2024+' windows are therefore both restricted to 2024-2026, which is disclosed as a remaining evidence gap below, not silently substituted for the old full-sample window.
existing_solution_comparison: Not a new mechanism: the exact reopening condition was named by the refuted card itself. reports/research/signal-cards/fundamentals-v1-manifest.json's amendment log (2026-09-24T05:20:00Z) states verbatim: 'usable session = first NYSE session after the 10-Q/10-K filing date, which usually lags the earnings press release (8-K item 2.02) by days to weeks; the card measures drift after the XBRL filing, the tradeable version with free data' -- i.e. the prior implementation itself flagged the 8-K timestamp as the correct, cheaper-to-test, tradable version, not built at the time for scope reasons. The 8-K Item-2.02 acceptance-timestamp table already exists locally (data/features/earnings_events/, built under a separate already-sourced task, docs/plan-earnings-text-forward-test-2026-09-22.zh.md) with the Eastern-time acceptanceDateTime handling already verified. No new signal-card mechanism, admission rule, cost convention, or placebo is introduced; only the visible_at join changes. Independent published evidence that announcement timing (not filing-date timing) is the economically load-bearing variable for tradable PEAD: Battalio & Mendenhall, 'Post-Earnings Announcement Drift: Timing and Liquidity Costs' (SSRN 920446, already source-carded in this repo as profit_route_challenge_20260921:pead_cost_counterpoint, quote 'We use the exact dates and times of earnings announcements'), reconfirmed live today (2026-09-28) via Crossref: 1993-2002 actual quote data, hedged-portfolio returns >=14%/yr after costs when trading immediately on the announcement rather than waiting until market close -- directly on point for why visible_at timing (not just SUE magnitude) can flip a PEAD result from unprofitable to profitable.
remaining_evidence_gap: (1) 8-K/2.02 acceptance-timestamp coverage is 2024-01-02 to 2026-09-17 only (2.7 years); the refuted filing-date card's 4,639 events over 2016-2026 cannot be reproduced under this timestamp, so this test necessarily has far fewer events and no true out-of-2024+ 'full' window -- a genuinely smaller, more recent-only sample, not a like-for-like re-run. (2) Matching each SUE-bearing fiscal quarter to its own 8-K/2.02 filing is done by nearest-preceding 8-K per CIK within a bounded window (implementation detail in candidate-manifest.json); a company that skips a standalone earnings 8-K (files results directly in the 10-Q/10-K, no separate 2.02 exhibit) will have no match and is dropped, not substituted with the old filing-date visible_at -- this could shrink the sample further and is reported as a coverage number in results.json, not hidden. (3) Independent literature (Subrahmanyam replication cited in the original card's own rationale) already found classic SUE-based PEAD ex-microcap is not significant (t=1.43) through Dec 2024 -- any admission here should still be read as a microcap-tilted, tier-1/2-scrutinized effect per that card's own caveat, not a rediscovery of a durable large-cap anomaly.
negative_experiments_checked: dir:pead_xbrl_sue_filing_date (refuted, reports/research/signal-cards/pead_sue_eps_event.json, checked via `uv run oc research directions check sue 8k earnings surprise pead`): CAR +0.71% at 20d (t=3.6, passes car_t_ge_3) but beats_redated=False (real 20bp-book excess_ann -3.9% vs the redated placebo's 20-seed mean excess_ann +4.6%..+8.8%, i.e. the real result is WORSE than dates picked at random) and book_positive_20bp=False (-3.9%/yr full window); only book_positive_20bp_recent=True (+1.5% in 2024+) passed. Admission rule (event_long, reports/research/signal-cards/fundamentals-v1-manifest.json) requires beats_redated AND t_dates>=3 AND book positive at 20bp in BOTH full and 2024+ windows -- this card failed two of three required legs and was rejected. This iteration changes only the visible_at leg the card's own amendment note named as the fix; it does not relax the admission rule, the cost convention, or the placebo. dir:pead_classic_sue_microcap_decay (evidence_too_weak, external UCLA/Subrahmanyam replication) is a separate, already-reviewed caveat folded into target_regime_and_horizon above, not re-litigated here. dir:earnings_8k_tone_next_day (refuted) is a different mechanism (LLM tone, next-day) and out of scope for this accounting-only stage.
cost_and_execution_assumptions: Unchanged from the refuted card and the fundamentals-v1 library: 10bp and 20bp per side on sum|dw|, close signal -> next open fill (signal_card.py's own forward_returns/book_returns), excess measured against the PIT universe equal weight. No new cost assumption, no order submission, no paper-trading path touched. Heavy computation (duckdb over data/features/daily_broad, universe_broad, sec_fundamentals_daily, earnings_events) runs through scripts/run_capped.sh --mem 1.8G with duckdb memory_limit <=1200MB, one job at a time, per the box's 4GB RAM / no-GPU constraint; this is the only heavy job running this session.
stop_condition: Admission rule reused verbatim from fundamentals-v1-manifest.json event_long: beats_redated AND t_dates>=3 at the primary horizon (20d) AND calendar-time book positive excess at 20bp in both the full (2024-2026, per the data-coverage gap above) and 2024+ windows. Any leg failing means the direction stays refuted under the 8-K timestamp too and no second-stage (DeepSeek tone/guidance overlay) work is queued. K1/K2 (docs/runbook-autonomous-round.zh.md section 5) are reported for information only, since this is a single-signal card, not a full sleeve compared against S3 -- they are not a substitute admission gate.

queries.query: crossref works 10.2139/ssrn.920446 Battalio Mendenhall post earnings announcement drift timing liquidity costs abstract

sources.claim: 另一篇 2006 年 PEAD 研究作者摘要采用精确公告时间和可成交报价，报告其 1993–2002 样本在多种成本假设下仍有扣费收益。
sources.market_and_period: US common stocks, actual NYSE/AMEX/Nasdaq quote data, 1993-2002 (Battalio & Mendenhall, 'Post-Earnings Announcement Drift: Timing and Liquidity Costs').
sources.applicability: Directly on point for why this iteration's only change (visible_at moved from the 10-Q/10-K filing date to the 8-K/2.02 announcement acceptance time) is the economically correct fix the refuted card named for itself: this paper's central finding is that trading on the exact announcement timestamp rather than a later, coarser timestamp is what recovers a positive after-cost PEAD return in its own sample.
sources.limitations: 2006 working paper on a 1993-2002 sample; does not establish that the effect is still tradable in 2024-2026 or in this project's universe/cost model -- that is exactly what this iteration's own backtest tests, not assumed from this citation.
sources.independent_replication: Reconfirmed live 2026-09-28 via a direct Crossref fetch of the same DOI record (title/authors/abstract match the 2026-09-21 saved snapshot); no third-party replication of the paper's own 14%/yr figure was sought or is claimed here.

cheapest_decisive_test.action: Build a new visible_at join (symbol, trade_date, sue_eps) from the existing sue_eps values (data/features/sec_fundamentals_daily) matched to each company's nearest-preceding 8-K/Item-2.02 acceptance timestamp (data/features/earnings_events), then run the unmodified open_composer/research/signal_card.py in event mode (threshold 2.0, top_n 3000, primary_horizon 20) against it, through scripts/run_capped.sh --mem 1.8G with duckdb memory_limit<=1200MB.
cheapest_decisive_test.pass_condition: event_long admission rule from fundamentals-v1-manifest.json: beats_redated AND t_dates>=3 at h=20 AND book positive excess at 20bp in both the full (2024-2026) and 2024+ windows.
cheapest_decisive_test.falsification_condition: Any one of: beats_redated=False, t_dates<3 at h=20, or 20bp book excess negative in either window -> refuted, same disposition as the filing-date version, no second-stage DeepSeek work queued.
